claims.text: The blog post title identifies 10 cloud infrastructure trends shaping 2027 and beyond.
This blog post was updated on 2026-09-15.
The post covers 2027's biggest cloud trends, including agentic infrastructure, hyperscaler AI spend, Kubernetes, IaC, DevSecOps, and platform engineering.
In 2027, AI agents are moving from writing code to operating infrastructure directly, with humans approving changes rather than authoring every one.
Hyperscaler capital spending is accelerating.
Kubernetes-for-AI adoption is accelerating.
Platform engineering adoption is accelerating.
Last year's edition of this blog post predicted a cloud-first, AI-driven decade.
Microsoft's Azure business crossed $100 billion in trailing revenue.
Google Cloud's backlog reached $514 billion.
AWS's AI business passed a $25 billion annualized run rate.
AWS's custom-silicon business passed a $25 billion annualized run rate.
The blog's 2026 predictions held up.
According to Gartner, by 2028 cloud-native platforms will serve as the foundation for more than 95% of new digital initiatives, up from less than 50% in 2023.
Gartner forecast that worldwide public cloud spending will exceed $1 trillion in 2027.
Gartner has described cloud as becoming, in its words, a business necessity by 2028.
McKinsey & Company's "In search of cloud value" report states that cloud value is driven by innovation, worth 5x more than cost savings.
McKinsey & Company's "In search of cloud value" report states an EBITDA uplift of 20-30% by 2030 for high-performing organizations.
McKinsey & Company's "In search of cloud value" report states that Asia leads in projected cloud value, followed by the US and Europe.

McKinsey & Company's "In search of cloud value" report states that high-ROI organizations excel by aligning cloud strategy with business priorities, building strong cloud foundations, and using modern operating models.
Pulumi Insights + Policies is a unified governance framework.
Hyperscalers are making the largest infrastructure investments in cloud history.
Hyperscalers' infrastructure investments are centered on AI workloads, inference, and high-performance compute.
AWS posted its fastest revenue growth since 2021.
AWS reported $42.2 billion in revenue in Q2 2026, up 37% year-over-year.
AWS's Q2 2026 growth accelerated from 28% growth the prior quarter.
AWS's AI business exceeded a $25 billion annualized revenue run rate.
AWS's chips business, which includes its custom Trainium and Graviton silicon, exceeded a $25 billion annualized revenue run rate.
AWS's AI business grew triple-digit percentages year-over-year.
AWS's chips business grew triple-digit percentages year-over-year.
Microsoft Azure's full fiscal-year 2026 revenue surpassed $100 billion for the first time.
This Azure revenue milestone was reported in Microsoft's fiscal Q4 2026, which ended June 30, 2026.
Azure revenue grew 43% year-over-year in fiscal Q4 2026, up from 40% the prior quarter.
Satya Nadella, Microsoft's chairman and CEO, said, "This year, Azure revenue surpassed $100 billion for the first time."
Google Cloud revenue rose 82% year-over-year to $24.8 billion in Q2 2026.
Google Cloud's backlog reached $514 billion, up from $106 billion a year earlier.
Alphabet raised its full-year 2026 capital expenditure guidance to $195-205 billion, up from an earlier $180-190 billion estimate.
Alphabet's earlier $180-190 billion capital expenditure estimate had itself already been raised twice this year.
Oracle reported FY2026 cloud revenue of $34.0 billion, up 39% year-over-year.
Oracle's remaining performance obligations reached $638 billion, up 363% year-over-year.
Oracle's remaining performance obligations growth was attributed to large-scale AI infrastructure contracts, including prepaid and customer-supplied GPU deals now totaling $75 billion.
Hybrid cloud will grow from $130B to $310-330B by 2030, according to ResearchAndMarkets.
87% of enterprises run workloads across multiple clouds, according to Mordor Intelligence.
Gartner predicts that 40% of enterprises will adopt hybrid compute architectures in mission-critical workflows by 2028, up from 8%.
In Pulumi's 2026 survey of 510 platform, DevOps, and product engineers, 64% run on AWS.
In Pulumi's 2026 survey of 510 platform, DevOps, and product engineers, 55% run on Google Cloud.
In Pulumi's 2026 survey of 510 platform, DevOps, and product engineers, 45% run on Azure.
In Pulumi's 2026 survey of 510 platform, DevOps, and product engineers, most surveyed teams run on more than one cloud.
As AI and regulatory requirements grow, organizations must deploy workloads across AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, on-prem, and edge while maintaining consistent security, compliance, and configuration.
According to Gartner, total worldwide AI spending, spanning software, hardware, and services, is forecast to reach $2.59 trillion in 2026, a 47% increase year-over-year.
IDC predicts that by 2027, half of enterprises will be using AI agents to redefine how humans and machines collaborate.
Gartner predicts that by 2028, over 50% of enterprises will use AI security platforms to secure third-party AI service usage and protect custom-built AI applications.
Gartner predicts total spending on securing AI will reach roughly $4.8 billion in 2027.

Carlie Idoine, VP Analyst at Gartner, said at the Gartner Data & Analytics Summit in Sydney, "[AI]... it doesn't deliver value on its own – AI needs to be tightly aligned with data, analytics, and governance to enable intelligent, adaptive decisions and actions across the organization."

According to Gartner, by 2026, 80% of large software engineering organizations will establish platform engineering teams as internal providers of reusable services, components, and tools for application delivery.
CNCF's Q1 2026 Technology Radar report with SlashData found 28% of surveyed organizations already have a dedicated platform engineering team.
CNCF's Q1 2026 Technology Radar report with SlashData found 35% of surveyed organizations are running a hybrid platform that combines existing developer platforms with specialized AI tooling.

Chris Aniszczyk, CTO of CNCF, said, "Cloud native platforms have reached a point where developers are not just experimenting but standardizing on CNCF projects that make software delivery reliable at scale."

Chris Aniszczyk, CTO of CNCF, said, "What's especially notable about this research is how organizations are extending those same platforms to support AI workloads, showing how cloud native is the base layer of powering the next era of applications."
Mid-size to large companies continue to invest in implementing platform engineering practices, with large tech companies as first adopters.
Gartner predicts that agentic AI deployment in IT operations grows from under 5% in 2025 to 70% by 2029.
Gartner predicts that human-in-the-loop requirements in IT operations workflows fall from 95% in 2025 to 40% by 2028.
Pulumi's 2026 survey of 510 platform, DevOps, and product engineers shows the same agentic shift starting inside real teams, with a gap between sentiment and practice.
In Pulumi's 2026 survey, 82% of respondents agree that AI and agents will meaningfully change how they write infrastructure within 12 months.
In Pulumi's 2026 survey, 63% of respondents say they trust agents to make production changes.
In Pulumi's 2026 survey, manual approval remains close to universal today despite 63% saying they trust agents to make production changes.
Pulumi's report describes the gap between stated trust in agents and actual guardrails as stated trust outrunning real guardrails.
In Pulumi's 2026 survey, teams expecting agents to generate half or more of their infrastructure code rise from 45% today to 52% within six months.
Pulumi Neo is built around a loop of proposing infrastructure changes, running previews, and executing approved updates with policy guardrails in place.
According to Mordor Intelligence, the global Kubernetes market is valued at USD 3.13 billion in 2026.
According to Mordor Intelligence, the global Kubernetes market is projected to reach USD 8.41 billion by 2031, a 21.85% CAGR.
The CNCF's Q3 2025 State of Cloud Native Development report puts cloud-native adoption among professional ML/AI developers at 41%.
The CNCF's Q3 2025 State of Cloud Native Development report finds 30% of backend developers now using Kubernetes directly, down from a peak of 36% in Q3 2023.
The CNCF report attributes the decline in backend developers directly using Kubernetes to the technology's growing maturity.
Kubernetes is evolving in response to AI demands, requiring low-latency execution closer to the user for inference workloads powered by LLMs and GPUs.
AI-powered coding assistants like GitHub Copilot, Claude Code, Cursor, and others have moved from novelty to everyday tooling for a large share of enterprise software teams.
According to Gartner, by 2028, 75% of enterprise software engineers will use dedicated AI code assistants.
According to Gartner, 63% of organizations are currently piloting, deploying or beginning to use AI code assistants.
The Model Context Protocol underwent a revision in July 2026.
The July 2026 revision of the Model Context Protocol is described by its maintainers as the largest revision of the protocol to date.
AWS shipped a general-availability MCP server for its Agent Toolkit.
Mirantis's Lens, a Kubernetes tooling vendor, has released a built-in MCP server.
Pulumi Agent Skills is a collection of infrastructure expertise packaged for use in AI coding assistants.

Pulumi Agent Skills teach tools such as Claude Code, Cursor, or Gemini CLI to reason about Pulumi projects, reducing hallucination and improving outputs based on real infrastructure conventions and practices.
Pulumi's Remote MCP Server provides infrastructure access that teams can combine with AI assistants to build secure, AI-driven workflows.
Cloud infrastructure is entering its most transformative era since the rise of Kubernetes.
Modern IaC, unified governance, reusable components, and policy frameworks are all core capabilities of the Pulumi Cloud platform.
